issues.legal_issue: The procedure for substituting a deceased defendant’s legal representatives applies only when the defendant dies while the suit is pending.
material_facts: The purchaser named as a defendant had died before the plaintiff filed the suit to challenge the sale deed.

The plaintiff first sought to bring the purchaser’s legal representatives on record through the procedure for substitution following a defendant’s death, and that application was rejected as not maintainable.
issues.conclusion: That substitution procedure was unavailable because the defendant died before the suit was filed.
issues.legal_principle: Order 22 Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure applies when a sole defendant or one of several defendants dies during the subsistence of the suit; it does not apply when the defendant died before institution of the suit.

predicates.civil_suit: The claimant brought a civil suit to obtain a judicial determination of a dispute.
predicates.defendant_died_before_filing: A defendant died before the claimant filed the suit.

issues.definition: When a defendant dies before a civil suit is filed, the procedure for substituting a defendant who dies during the suit does not apply.

issues.legal_issue: An earlier rejection of an application as procedurally unavailable does not bar a later application for the same relief when the earlier application was not decided on its merits.
material_facts: The plaintiff’s first application to bring the deceased defendant’s legal representatives on record was rejected as not maintainable because the defendant had died before the suit was filed.
The court did not adjudicate on the merits of whether the legal representatives should be joined.
The plaintiff later applied to join them through a procedure available for adding parties.
issues.conclusion: The earlier rejection did not operate as res judicata and did not bar the later application.
issues.legal_principle: A procedural rejection that makes no adjudication on the merits does not preclude a later maintainable application seeking the same relief. The Court relied on Order 1 Rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure and distinguished cases concerning death during a pending proceeding, including Banwari Lal v. Balbir Singh and Arora Enterprises Ltd. v. Indubhushan Obhan.

rule.if: civil_suit and earlier_application_rejected_as_unmaintainable and no_merits_determination and later_application_seeks_same_relief

predicates.civil_suit: The claimant brought a civil suit to obtain a judicial determination of a dispute.
predicates.earlier_application_rejected_as_unmainta: A court rejected an earlier application because the procedure invoked was unavailable in the circumstances.
predicates.no_merits_determination: The court did not decide the substance of the requested relief.
predicates.later_application_seeks_same_relief: The claimant later applied for the same substantive relief through a procedurally available route.

issues.definition: If an earlier application in a civil suit was rejected as procedurally unavailable without a decision on the merits, a later application seeking the same relief is not barred merely because it seeks that relief again.

issues.legal_issue: The legal representatives of a purchaser who died before a suit challenging the sale may be added as parties when their presence is needed to resolve the dispute, subject to limitation.
material_facts: The suit sought to set aside a sale deed, and the purchaser named as a defendant had died before the suit was filed.
The purchaser’s legal representatives had a direct interest in the property and were necessary for effective and complete adjudication of the dispute.
The plaintiff asserted that he did not know of the purchaser’s death when filing the suit.

The earlier application under the procedure for substitution after a defendant’s death had been rejected as not maintainable, and the later application to add the legal representatives had also been rejected.
The Supreme Court directed that the legal representatives be brought on record, leaving limitation issues for determination during trial.
issues.conclusion: The legal representatives must be impleaded as parties, subject to the limitation plea being decided during the trial.
issues.legal_principle: Order 1 Rule 10(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure gives the court discretion to add a person whose presence is necessary to effectually and completely adjudicate all questions in the suit; Sections 151 and 153 support the court’s power to advance justice and correct procedural defects. Section 21(1) of the Limitation Act, 1963, including its proviso concerning a mistake made in good faith, and Order 7 Rule 6 of the Code make limitation a matter to be considered in the case. The Court relied on Ram Prasad Dagduram v. Vijay Kumar Motilal Mirakhanwala, Bhagwan Swaroop v. Mool Chand, Karuppaswamy v. C. Ramamurthy and Banwari Lal v. Balbir Singh, and emphasized that procedural rules should advance rather than impede justice.

predicates.civil_suit_to_challenge_transfer: A claimant brought a civil suit seeking to challenge a transfer of property.
predicates.purchaser_died_before_filing: The purchaser whose transfer is challenged died before the suit was filed.
predicates.legal_representatives_have_direct_intere: The deceased purchaser’s legal representatives have a direct interest in the property or the outcome of the suit.
predicates.their_presence_needed_for_complete_adjud: The court cannot effectively and completely resolve the questions in the suit without the legal representatives.

issues.definition: When a property-transfer challenge requires the presence of the deceased purchaser’s directly interested legal representatives for complete adjudication, they are added as parties while limitation remains for determination.
